services.name: LOTD
services.description: `LOTD` is a single-service monolith backing a padel/badminton scoring app — it handles board creation by game type, Americano session pairing generation, round running with adjustable points-per-round, and leaderboard computation. All logic sits in one `service` layer with no separate API layer.

violations.title: `openStartAmericano` combines roster selection, session creation, and runner navigation
violations.content: `openStartAmericano` spans 74 lines with 20 statements and a nested `sync`/`drawRoster` pair, and reaches across at least four responsibility areas: it builds and maintains roster-selection state (`activePlayers`, `drawRoster`, `sync`), primes browser audio (`ensureAudio`), renders the sheet (`el`, `openSheet` twice), performs the backend write (`attempt` → `api.createPadelSession`, plus `api.localToday` for the session date), then reloads (`refresh`) and immediately navigates by opening another modal (`openSessionRunner`). The Americano pairing/roster rules are inseparable from the DOM and the API call, so none of it can be tested or reused without opening a sheet.
violations.fixPrompt: Split `openStartAmericano` in the `sportScoreError` UI module. Extract the roster-selection state machine (currently `drawRoster` + `sync`) into a standalone controller that exposes the chosen player list and validity, move session creation (`api.createPadelSession` plus the date defaulting from `api.localToday`) into a padel-session service function, and have the sheet only render and dispatch. Let the caller — not the create path — decide whether to open `openSessionRunner` after a session is created, so creating a session and navigating to the runner are independently testable.

violations.title: `openPlayers` renders the roster and performs three separate mutations
violations.content: `openPlayers` is 48 lines at nesting depth 3 and owns a nested `draw` helper plus three distinct write flows in the same closure: add (`attempt` → `api.addPlayer`), archive (`attempt` → `api.deletePlayer`) and restore (`attempt` → `api.restorePlayer`), each followed by its own `refresh` (3 calls) and re-`draw` (4 calls). Rendering the active/archived lists, escaping names (`esc` ×4 inside `draw`), and three unrelated persistence operations with their own confirmation/refresh handling all live in one function, so no mutation path can be exercised without instantiating the sheet.
violations.fixPrompt: In the `sportScoreError` UI module, reduce `openPlayers` to rendering plus event dispatch. Move the add/archive/restore handlers into small named functions (for example `addPlayerFlow`, `archivePlayerFlow`, `restorePlayerFlow`) that each wrap one `api` call with `attempt` and return a result, and have the sheet re-render from a single place instead of interleaving `refresh` and `draw` calls inside each handler.

violations.title: `api` module is largely a pass-through wrapper around `call`
violations.content: Of the 23 functions in `api`, twelve are two-line one-liners that do nothing but forward to `api.call`: `createLeaderboard`, `renameLeaderboard`, `deleteLeaderboard`, `addPlayer`, `deletePlayer`, `restorePlayer`, `undoLast`, `editLoser`, `deleteGame`, `undoLastSports`, `editSportsScore`, `deleteSportsGame`. `listLeaderboards` likewise just forwards to `get`. None of these add validation, transformation, or error handling — the error handling lives in the UI's `attempt` wrapper instead — so the layer adds a name per endpoint and nothing else, while `logGame`, `logSportsGame` and `createPadelSession` are inconsistent in that they at least default the date via `localToday`. The indirection obscures that every call site is really just an action string plus a payload.
violations.fixPrompt: Give the `api` module a reason to exist or collapse it. Either (a) make the wrappers meaningful — validate and normalize payloads, map backend error responses into typed client errors, and absorb the retry/lock handling currently done by `attempt` in the UI module — or (b) drop the twelve pure pass-throughs (`createLeaderboard`, `renameLeaderboard`, `deleteLeaderboard`, `addPlayer`, `deletePlayer`, `restorePlayer`, `undoLast`, `editLoser`, `deleteGame`, `undoLastSports`, `editSportsScore`, `deleteSportsGame`) in favour of a single typed `call(action, payload)` with a discriminated action union. Whichever you choose, apply the date defaulting used by `logGame`, `logSportsGame` and `createPadelSession` consistently.

violations.title: `combinedAllTime` aggregates the backend's board payload from inside the UI module
violations.content: `combinedAllTime` uses no state of its own: it pulls the raw board payload out of the `api` module via `get()` and walks the card-game and sports-game collections to produce combined all-time standings, then hands the result to `spotlightHTML` for rendering. The aggregation rule (how card wins and sports wins are merged into one ranking) is domain logic living in a presentation module, operating entirely over data owned by `api` and shaped by the `admin` backend, so any change to the payload structure silently breaks the leaderboard with no signal.
violations.fixPrompt: Move `combinedAllTime` out of the `sportScoreError` UI module and next to the board data it consumes — either into the `api` module as a typed selector over the loaded board, or into a shared standings module that takes an explicit, typed board argument instead of calling `api.get()` internally. Leave `spotlightHTML` responsible only for turning the returned rows into markup.

violations.title: Americano courts/rounds bounds repeated as bare literals in `readCourts` and `readRounds`
violations.content:
`readCourts` clamps with `Math.max(1, Math.min(6, ...))` and `readRounds` clamps with `Math.max(1, Math.min(60, ...))`. The same `6` and `60` are already hardcoded in the input markup fifteen lines above — `min="1" max="6"` for courts (`js/app.js:587`) and `min="1" max="60"` for rounds (`js/app.js:588`).

Nothing names what 6 and 60 are (max courts on a padel night, max rounds in a session) or why those are the limits. Because the bound lives in two unrelated places — an HTML attribute string and a `Math.min` call — they can silently drift: raising the courts input to `max="8"` would leave `readCourts` quietly clamping an 8-court night back down to 6 with no error shown to the user. This is the same duplication pattern already reported for the points-per-round bounds in `readPoints`, but for a distinct pair of numbers.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, extract the Americano session bounds into named module-level constants near `GT_GROUPS`, e.g. `const MAX_COURTS = 6;` and `const MAX_ROUNDS = 60;` (add a short comment saying what each limit represents). Use them both in the `openStartAmericano` markup (`max="${MAX_COURTS}"` on `#courts`, `max="${MAX_ROUNDS}"` on `#rounds`) and in `readCourts`/`readRounds` so the input attributes and the clamp can never disagree.
violations.snippet:
const readCourts = () => Math.max(1, Math.min(6, Number(courtsEl.value) || 1));
  const readRounds = (n, c) => Math.max(1, Math.min(60, Number(roundsEl.value) || suggestedRounds(n, c) || 1));

violations.title: `loadBoards` also resolves and reassigns the active `boardId`
violations.content:
`loadBoards` reads as "fetch the list of boards", and its first line does exactly that. But it then also reads `localStorage` under `LAST_BOARD` and reassigns the module-level `boardId` — it decides which board the whole UI is currently showing, which is board-*selection* state, not board-*list* state.

The scope is wider than the name suggests, and the extra behaviour is destructive: any call to `loadBoards()` silently discards the currently selected board and resets it to the remembered one (or `boards[0]`). Today the only caller is `refresh()` (`js/app.js:135`), where that reset is harmless because it re-validates the remembered id. But `switchBoard` deliberately calls only `loadBoard()` (`js/app.js:142`) precisely to avoid this — so a future caller that reaches for `loadBoards()` to pick up a newly created board would silently yank the user back to a different board mid-session.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, either rename `loadBoards` to something that states both effects (e.g. `loadBoardsAndSelect`), or split the selection out: have `loadBoards` only assign `boards`, add a separate `selectRememberedBoard()` that resolves `boardId` from `LAST_BOARD` with a fallback to `boards[0]?.id`, and call both from `refresh()`.

violations.title: `get` has no failure tracking or fail-fast path when Supabase is down
violations.content:
`get` is the shared read primitive for every Supabase REST call, and `call` (lines 206-215) is the equivalent for the admin edge function. Neither tracks failure rates nor short-circuits after repeated failures — each invocation issues a fresh `fetch` regardless of how many consecutive calls have just failed.

This matters because `get` is not called once per page load: `refresh()` re-runs `loadBoard()` after every write, and the Americano round-runner calls `await refresh()` on each individual match log. When Supabase is unavailable (outage, expired key, offline device), every user interaction fires a full fan-out of requests that are all certain to fail, each waiting out the full network timeout before surfacing the generic `Couldn't reach the server` error. The user experiences a long hang per tap instead of an immediate, clear offline state, and the client keeps hammering the failing backend.

The blast radius is bounded compared to a server-side integration — a browser tab cannot exhaust a shared connection pool — which is why this is low rather than medium. But a lightweight breaker (track consecutive failures in a module-level counter; once a threshold is crossed, reject immediately until a cooldown elapses or one probe request succeeds) would both fail fast for the user and stop the retry storm.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/api.js`, add a small module-level circuit breaker shared by `get` and `call`. Track consecutive failures (network rejections and `5xx`/`429` responses only — do not count `4xx` client errors) in a counter. When the counter reaches a threshold (e.g. 4), open the breaker: subsequent calls to `get`/`call` should reject immediately with a distinct "service unavailable, retrying shortly" error rather than issuing a `fetch`. After a cooldown (e.g. 15-30s), move to half-open and allow a single probe request through; a success resets the counter and closes the breaker, a failure re-opens it. Make sure the UI distinguishes the breaker-open error from a normal request failure so users see an offline state instead of a generic message.

violations.title: `padel_sessions` is fetched in full with no `limit`, though only the newest row is ever used
violations.content:
The `padel_sessions` query inside `loadBoard` uses `order=created_at.desc` but no `limit` or `Range` header, so every call materializes **every** Americano session ever created on the board into `data.padelSessions`. The array has no cap and grows by one entry per padel night for the life of the leaderboard.

The waste is total: the only consumer of the collection is `latestSession()` in `js/app.js:548`, which reads `(data?.padelSessions ?? [])[0]` — the single newest row. Every other row is downloaded, parsed, and retained purely to be discarded. And because `refresh()` calls `loadBoard()` after every write — including after *each individual match* logged in the Americano round-runner (`openSessionRunner`, `js/app.js:732`) — a single padel night re-downloads the entire session history dozens of times.

Each row also carries a `roster` array, so the payload grows with both session count and roster size. Adding `&limit=1` makes this collection constant-size and matches exactly what the UI consumes; if a session list is wanted later, page it explicitly.
violations.fixPrompt: In `loadBoard` in `js/api.js`, bound the `padel_sessions` query. Since the only consumer is `latestSession()` in `js/app.js` (which reads index `0`), append `&limit=1` to the query string — or a small explicit page size such as `&limit=20` if a future session list is anticipated — so `data.padelSessions` cannot grow without bound as the board accumulates Americano nights. Keep the existing `order=created_at.desc` so the newest session is still first.
violations.snippet: get(`padel_sessions?select=id,game_date,roster,courts,rounds,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=created_at.desc`),

violations.title: Failed-passcode log omits the `ts` field every other log line carries
violations.content:
This module has two log call sites and they emit different record shapes. The `log` helper defined at line 131 emits `{ at, action, ip, ok, ts, ...extra }` — including an ISO `ts` timestamp — and is used for every success and for the catch-all error path at line 421. The wrong-passcode log on line 125 is written inline instead, emitting `{ at: 'admin', action, ip, ok: false, error: 'wrong passcode' }` with no `ts`.

The inline call sits before `log` is defined (the helper is declared at line 131, after the passcode check returns), so the divergence is structural rather than accidental. The practical effect is that the one log line recording authentication failures — the records most likely to be queried during an incident or brute-force investigation — is the only one missing the timestamp field. Any log query or dashboard that filters, sorts, or buckets on `ts` silently drops auth failures from its results, and a mixed-shape stream forces consumers to special-case `ts` as optional.

Hoisting the `log` helper above the passcode check (it only depends on `action` and `ip`, both available by line 120) and calling `log(false, { error: 'wrong passcode' })` makes all three call sites emit one consistent schema.
violations.fixPrompt: In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, move the `log` helper currently defined at line 131 so it is declared immediately after `action`, `passcode`, and `payload` are destructured from the body (around line 120), before the `passcodeMatches` check. Then replace the inline `console.log(JSON.stringify({ at: 'admin', action, ip, ok: false, error: 'wrong passcode' }))` on line 125 with `log(false, { error: 'wrong passcode' })` so the failed-passcode record carries the same `ts` field as every other log line. Leave the `db` client creation where it is — only the `log` helper moves.
violations.snippet: console.log(JSON.stringify({ at: 'admin', action, ip, ok: false, error: 'wrong passcode' }));

violations.title: Module-level `editing` and `confirming` are reset across `await` boundaries in the history handler
violations.content:
The history rows click handler mutates the module-level UI state `editing` and `confirming` both synchronously (lines 806, 820, 826) and *after* awaiting a network round-trip (lines 809, 818, 824: `if (await attempt(...)) { editing = null; await refresh(); draw(); }`).

Because the handler is `async` and the list stays interactive while the request is in flight, a second click can run to completion before the first resumes. Concrete interleaving: the user taps "save score" on row A (request in flight), then taps "edit" on row B — `editing` is set to B and `draw()` renders B's editor; when A's request resolves it unconditionally executes `editing = null`, silently closing B's editor and discarding whatever was typed into it. The same applies to `confirming`: a delete confirmation opened for one row is wiped by an unrelated in-flight request resolving at line 809 or 818.

The state is written after the `await` without re-checking that it still refers to the interaction that started the request, which is exactly the lost-update shape the rule targets. Note this is distinct from the `data`/`boardId` staleness already tracked separately — here the clobbered state is the per-row editor selection.
violations.fixPrompt: In the history rows click handler in `js/app.js` (around lines 803-827), capture the state token the interaction owns before awaiting and only clear it if it is still current. For example, in the `d.newloser` branch capture `const owned = editing;` (or the row id) before `await attempt(...)`, and after it resolves do `if (editing === owned) editing = null;` instead of the unconditional `editing = null`. Apply the same guard to `confirming` in the `d.yes` branch. Alternatively, disable the row's buttons (or set an in-flight flag that early-returns at the top of the handler) for the duration of the request so a second interaction cannot start while one is pending.

violations.title: `create_padel_session` validates the board and roster, then inserts in a separate query
violations.content:
`create_padel_session` performs two read queries — the board's `game_types` (lines 396-400) and every roster player's `leaderboard_id`/`archived` state (lines 403-408) — and then inserts the session in a third, unrelated statement (lines 410-411). There is no transaction and no re-validation, so both checks act on a snapshot that can be stale by the time the insert runs.

A concurrent `delete_player` that archives a roster member (line 201) or hard-deletes them (line 206) between the read and the insert produces a session whose `roster` array contains an archived or non-existent player id. `roster` is a plain array column, so no foreign key catches it — unlike `sports_games`, which has the composite FK backstop mentioned at line 323. The session is then created successfully and the runner in `js/app.js` will generate pairings that include a player who no longer exists, and every subsequent `log_sports_game` for that pairing fails the `archived` check at line 320 with no way to repair the session.

The same window lets a concurrent `rename_leaderboard` remove `padel` from `game_types` after the check at line 400 passes.
violations.fixPrompt: Make `create_padel_session` in `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts` atomic with respect to its validation. Preferred fix: move the whole case into a Postgres function invoked via `db.rpc(...)` that re-checks `leaderboards.game_types` and the roster players' `leaderboard_id`/`archived` state inside the same transaction as the `padel_sessions` insert, returning a well-typed error when a check fails. If an RPC is not desirable, add a database-level guard instead — e.g. a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `padel_sessions` that validates every id in `roster` against `players` for the same `leaderboard_id` with `archived = false` — so the check cannot be bypassed by an interleaved `delete_player`.

violations.title: `log_sports_game` checks players are active and in the session roster, then inserts separately
violations.content:
`log_sports_game` reads the players' `leaderboard_id`/`archived` state (lines 315-320) and, for session rounds, the session's `roster` (lines 328-334), then inserts the row in a separate statement at lines 337-338. Between the reads and the insert a concurrent `delete_player` can set `archived = true` (line 201), so a round is recorded against an archived player even though line 320 exists specifically to prevent that.

The inline comment at lines 322-323 relies on "the composite FK is the final backstop", but that FK only enforces the session/board relationship — it does not re-check `archived`, so nothing at the database level catches this interleaving. The resulting row then feeds `v_padel_standings` and `v_sport_standings`, resurrecting an archived player in the standings, and `delete_player`'s archive-vs-delete decision for that player was itself made on a count taken before this insert.

This window is materially wider during an Americano session, where the runner in `js/app.js:720-733` posts rounds in rapid succession while an admin may be editing the player list.
violations.fixPrompt: Enforce the `archived` and roster invariants atomically for `log_sports_game` in `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`. Best option: perform the insert through a Postgres function (`db.rpc(...)`) that re-verifies, in the same transaction as the `INSERT INTO sports_games`, that every named player belongs to `leaderboard_id`, is not archived, and (when `session_id` is set) appears in that session's `roster`. Alternatively add a `BEFORE INSERT` trigger on `sports_games` that raises a clear exception when any of `a1`,`a2`,`b1`,`b2` references an archived player, so the pre-check in the handler becomes an early-exit optimisation rather than the sole guarantee. Keep the existing checks for fast, friendly error messages and map the database exception back to the same wording.

violations.title: Mock `undoLast` returns `null` on a no-op while every other write returns a row
violations.content: `undoLast` in the mock backend returns `null` when `gamesOf(id)` is empty (`if (!last) return null;`) but a `{ id }` object when a game was actually removed, and the live path (`call('undo_last', ...)`) resolves to whatever the server returns for the deleted row. The caller — the undo button wired up in `showPecundang` via `attempt(null, () => api.undoLast(boardId, LOSER_WORD))` in `js/app.js` — treats any non-throwing result as success and calls `refresh()`, so a no-op undo is indistinguishable from a real one and the user is told the game was rolled back when nothing changed. `undoLastSports` (lines 151–154) has the identical shape. A sentinel `null` mixed with a payload object hides the "nothing to undo" case instead of surfacing it as an error the UI can show.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/api.js`, make the mock `undoLast` and `undoLastSports` signal the empty case explicitly instead of returning `null`: either `throw new Error('nothing to undo')` (matching how the live Edge Function reports a failed undo), or keep the return type uniform and have the caller in `js/app.js` check for a missing row before reporting success. Whichever is chosen, ensure both mock functions and the live `call(...)` path agree on the shape so `attempt(...)` cannot report a no-op as a successful undo.

violations.title: `drawTeams` rebuilds the `assigned()` array inside a per-player `.filter()` callback
violations.content:
`drawTeams` calls the `assigned()` helper — which allocates a fresh `[...a, ...b]` array on every invocation — three separate times per redraw, and critically once *per player* inside the `act.filter((p) => !assigned().includes(p.id))` callback on line 487. So rendering the pool allocates one throwaway array per active player and then does a linear `.includes` scan over it, making the pool render O(players × sideSize) with an allocation per player instead of O(players) with none.

The fix is mechanical: hoist a single `const taken = new Set([...a, ...b])` at the top of `drawTeams` and use `taken.has(p.id)` plus `taken.size` for the `need`/`full` computations on lines 484 and 486. This also removes the two redundant `assigned()` allocations on those lines.

This fires on every sport switch, every chip tap, and every player removal in the racquet-log sheet. Rosters are small so the wall-clock cost is minor — hence low severity — but it is the exact array-with-`.includes`-in-a-loop pattern a `Set` resolves, and the per-iteration array construction makes it worse than a plain repeated scan.
violations.fixPrompt: In `drawTeams` inside `openLogSport` in `js/app.js`, replace the repeated `assigned()` calls with a single `Set` built once per redraw. At the top of `drawTeams`, add `const taken = new Set([...a, ...b]);`. Then use `taken.size` in place of `assigned().length` for both the `need` calculation and the `full` calculation, and change the pool filter from `act.filter((p) => !assigned().includes(p.id))` to `act.filter((p) => !taken.has(p.id))`. Leave the `assigned` helper itself in place if it is used elsewhere.

violations.title: `LOTD` is an API server with no `api` layer
violations.content:
`LOTD` is declared as an `api-server` but the only architectural layer present is `service`. An API server is normally expected to expose an `api` layer (route definitions, request parsing/validation, response serialization) sitting in front of a `service` layer that holds business logic.

With the `api` layer absent, HTTP concerns and domain logic are collapsed into the same units. In a scoring app like this — board creation, Americano pairing generation, round running, leaderboard computation — that means the pairing/scoring rules are reachable only through whatever HTTP surface wraps them, and request shape changes cannot be made without touching domain code (and vice versa). It also removes the natural seam where request validation, versioning, and consistent error/response envelopes would live, which is why several other API-contract concerns have nowhere to be enforced.

Note: this finding is derived from the declared service metadata (`type: api-server`, `layers: service`) rather than from reading the 5 source files, which were not accessible during this analysis.
violations.fixPrompt: In the `LOTD` codebase, introduce an explicit `api` layer separated from the existing service layer. Move HTTP route definitions, request parsing and validation, status-code selection, and response serialization out of the service modules into dedicated route/controller modules (for example an `api/` or `routes/` directory). Leave the service modules holding only domain logic — board creation, Americano pairing generation, round running, points-per-round handling, and leaderboard computation — with plain function signatures that take and return domain values rather than HTTP request/response objects. The service layer should not import any HTTP framework types. Once the seam exists, use it as the single place to apply request validation and a consistent response/error envelope across all endpoints.

violations.title: `admin` request handler is a god function handling routing, auth, validation, and persistence
violations.content: The exported handler attributed to `corsHeaders` in `admin` concentrates the entire backend surface in one body: it builds CORS headers, dispatches every action, authenticates via `passcodeMatches`, validates input (`isId` called 17 times, `isIsoDate` 6 times, `isScore` 4 times, `cleanGameTypes`/`cleanPoints` twice each), applies game rules through `scoreError`, computes defaults with `utcToday`, and performs the persistence calls — across a 424-line module with only 9 functions. It even recurses into itself. This spans at least four distinct responsibility areas (transport, authn, validation, business rules + data access), which makes any single action impossible to unit-test or reuse in isolation and guarantees merge conflicts whenever any endpoint changes.
violations.fixPrompt: Split the monolithic handler in the `admin` function into a thin transport layer plus per-action handlers. Extract a `withCors` wrapper that only builds/attaches CORS headers, a `requirePasscode` guard that runs `passcodeMatches` once, and a dispatch table mapping each action name (`createLeaderboard`, `renameLeaderboard`, `deleteLeaderboard`, `addPlayer`, `deletePlayer`, `restorePlayer`, `logGame`, `undoLast`, `editLoser`, `deleteGame`, `logSportsGame`, `createPadelSession`, `undoLastSports`, `editSportsScore`, `deleteSportsGame`) to its own small function. Each action function should receive an already-validated payload from a per-action validator so `isId`, `isIsoDate`, `isScore`, `cleanGameTypes`, and `cleanPoints` are no longer scattered through one body.

violations.title: `admin` handler performs data access inline with no repository layer
violations.content: The single `admin` handler executes its persistence operations directly inside the request-handling body — there is no service or repository module between the HTTP entry point and the datastore (the module has only one import and no data-access collaborators). Business rules (`scoreError`, `cleanPoints`) and storage operations are interleaved in the same function, so the write paths for leaderboards, players, card games, sports games, and padel sessions cannot be exercised, mocked, or reused without going through an HTTP request.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce a data-access layer for the `admin` function — e.g. `leaderboardRepo`, `playerRepo`, `gameRepo`, and `padelSessionRepo` modules exposing intention-revealing operations (`insertGame`, `deleteSportsGame`, `createSession`, …). Move every direct datastore call out of the request handler into these repositories, and have the handler call a service function that composes validation, business rules, and repository calls.

violations.title: Sport scoring rules are hardcoded inside `scoreError`
violations.content: `scoreError(sport, a, b, padelTarget)` encodes the per-sport win conditions directly in branching logic (first-to-21 / win-by-2 / cap-30 style rules for badminton, padel target points, and per-sport score bounds) across 21 lines with 9 statements and nested conditions. Adding a sport, changing a cap, or supporting a variant format requires editing and redeploying code, and the same rule set already has to be mirrored on the client. These are configuration values, not control flow.
violations.fixPrompt: Replace the per-sport `if`/`switch` branches in `scoreError` with a declarative rules table, e.g. `const SPORT_RULES = { badminton: { target: 21, winBy: 2, cap: 30 }, padel: { target: null /* from session */, winBy: 1 }, ... }`, and make `scoreError` a generic validator that looks the rule up by sport name and applies `target`/`winBy`/`cap`/`maxScore` uniformly. Source the table from configuration (or the board record) so new sports and adjusted point targets do not require a code change.

violations.title: Adding or changing a sport requires edits in lockstep across client and server
violations.content: The sport/game-type discriminator is switched on in many places that must all be updated together: `scoreError` and `cleanGameTypes` in `admin`, and `sportScoreError` (client-side score validation), `boardTypes`, `hasType`, `hasAnyRacquet`, `isPadelBoard`, `gameTypePickerHTML`, `readGameTypes`, `drawTypes`, `sportTablesHTML`, and the padel-specific branches of `render` in the UI module. The scoring rules in particular exist twice — once in `scoreError` on the server and once in `sportScoreError` on the client — so a rule change that is applied in only one place silently produces a client that accepts scores the server rejects (or vice versa).
violations.fixPrompt: Extract a shared `sports` definition module consumed by both the `admin` backend and the UI: a single table keyed by sport name holding display label, team size, racquet flag, default points, and scoring rule. Rewrite `scoreError` (server) and `sportScoreError` (client) as thin wrappers over one shared `validateScore` implementation, and derive `boardTypes`, `hasType`, `hasAnyRacquet`, `isPadelBoard`, `gameTypePickerHTML`, and `drawTypes` from that table instead of hardcoding sport names in each.

violations.title: UI module mixes rendering, sheets, audio, export, and domain logic in 1219 lines
violations.content: The `sportScoreError` module holds 68 functions covering unrelated concerns: score validation (`sportScoreError`), DOM helpers (`el`, `esc`, `esc2`, `pct`), board metadata (`boardName`, `boardTypes`, `boardPoints`, `isPadelBoard`), sheet/modal UI (`openSheet`, `openPasscode`, `openNewBoard`, `openRenameBoard`, `openDeleteBoard`, `openPlayers`, `openLog`, `openLogSport`, `openGames`), padel session logic (`openStartAmericano`, `openSessionRunner`, `padelRowsFromGames`, `latestSession`, `sessionGames`), audio/roasting (`ensureAudio`, `playLoserSound`, `roastFor`, `showPecundang`), CSV export (`doExport`), leaderboard computation (`combinedAllTime`), and HTML generation (`spotlightHTML`, `sportTablesHTML`, `padelTableHTML`, `rowsHTML`, `tableHTML`, `render`). Any feature — a new sport, a new modal, an audio tweak — lands in this one file, so it changes for many unrelated reasons and appears in nearly every commit.
violations.fixPrompt: Split the `sportScoreError` module along its natural seams: `dom.js` (`el`, `esc`, `esc2`, `pct`, `openSheet`), `board.js` (`boardName`, `boardTypes`, `boardPoints`, `hasType`, `hasAnyRacquet`, `isPadelBoard`, `activePlayers`, `archivedPlayers`, `nameOf`), `sheets/` with one file per modal (`board-sheets.js`, `players-sheet.js`, `log-sheets.js`, `games-sheet.js`), `padel.js` (`openStartAmericano`, `openSessionRunner`, `padelRowsFromGames`, `latestSession`, `sessionGames`, padel HTML), `loser-fx.js` (`ensureAudio`, `playLoserSound`, `roastFor`, `showPecundang`), `export.js` (`doExport`), and `render.js` (the HTML builders plus `render`). Keep a small entry module that wires state, `refresh`, and event handlers.

violations.title: `openLogSport` orchestrates form state, validation, API writes, and side effects
violations.content: `openLogSport` spans 132 lines and 31 statements with nested inner functions (`drawTypes`, `slots`, `drawTeams`, `sync`) and reaches into `activePlayers`, `ensureAudio`, `el`, `openSheet`, `localToday`, `boardPoints`, `hasType`, `sportScoreError`, `attempt`, `logSportsGame`, `refresh`, `showPecundang`, and `undoLastSports`. It builds markup, manages team-slot selection state, validates scores, writes to the backend, triggers the loser sound/roast, and handles undo — five distinct responsibility areas in one closure, none of which can be tested or reused separately.
violations.fixPrompt: Break `openLogSport` into: a `sportLogFormHTML` builder for the markup, a `createTeamSelection` helper owning slot/roster state and the `slots`/`drawTeams`/`drawTypes` renderers, a `validateSportEntry` function wrapping `sportScoreError` and `boardPoints`, and a `submitSportGame` function that performs the `logSportsGame` call plus `refresh`, `showPecundang`, and undo handling. `openLogSport` should be reduced to wiring those pieces to the sheet.

violations.title: `openLog` mixes markup, selection state, submission, and loser effects
violations.content: `openLog` is 102 lines and 22 statements, calling `activePlayers`, `localToday`, `ensureAudio`, `el`, `openSheet` (twice), `esc`, `drawChips`, `sync` (3×), `nameOf`, `attempt` (2×), `logGame`, `refresh` (2×), `showPecundang`, and `undoLast`. It renders the sheet, maintains chip selection state, validates the entry, writes the game, plays the loser sound, and drives the undo confirmation flow — several unrelated responsibilities in one function.
violations.fixPrompt: Extract from `openLog` a `cardLogFormHTML` markup builder, a `createChipSelection` helper owning the chip state and `drawChips`/`sync`, and a `submitCardGame` function handling `logGame`, `refresh`, `showPecundang`, and the `undoLast` confirmation. Leave `openLog` responsible only for opening the sheet and wiring handlers.

violations.title: `openGames` combines list rendering, inline editing, and three delete/edit flows at 6 levels of nesting
violations.content: `openGames` is 92 lines with nesting depth 6, embedding `confirmRow`, `cardRow`, `sportRow`, and `draw`, and calling `attempt` 3×, `editLoser`, `editSportsScore`, `deleteGame`, `deleteSportsGame`, `sportScoreError`, `boardPoints`, and `refresh` 3×. One function renders two different row types, runs inline edit validation, and performs four distinct mutations with their own confirmation states. The nesting alone makes the control flow hard to follow and the mutation paths untestable.
violations.fixPrompt: Split `openGames` into a `gamesListHTML` renderer that delegates to standalone `cardRow`, `sportRow`, and `confirmRow` builders (moved to module scope), and a `gameMutations` set of small functions — `applyLoserEdit`, `applySportScoreEdit`, `removeCardGame`, `removeSportsGame` — each doing its own validation via `sportScoreError`/`boardPoints` and calling `refresh` once. Flatten the nested callbacks by using a single delegated click handler keyed on `data-action`.

violations.title: `render` is an 84-line, 35-statement function driving the whole page
violations.content: `render` reads unlock state via `isUnlocked`, branches on board type through `isPadelBoard`, `hasType` (3×) and `hasAnyRacquet` (2×), assembles six different HTML fragments (`padelSpotlightHTML`, `spotlightHTML`, `padelSessionBanner`, `padelTableHTML` 2×, `tableHTML`, `sportTablesHTML`), escapes strings inline with `esc`, and additionally opens a modal by calling `openSessionRunner`. Triggering a session-runner sheet from a render function couples display to navigation and makes re-rendering produce side effects.
violations.fixPrompt: Reduce `render` to composing already-built fragments: extract a `buildViewModel` step that resolves board type, unlock state, and which sections apply, then a `pageHTML(viewModel)` builder, then a small `mount` step that assigns markup and binds handlers. Move the `openSessionRunner` invocation out of `render` into the event handler or state transition that should actually open the runner, so rendering is side-effect free and idempotent.

violations.title: `openSessionRunner` owns session state, round math, rendering, and score submission
violations.content: `openSessionRunner` runs 91 lines with nested `mapGames` (15 lines) and `draw` (39 lines) helpers. Inside one closure it derives the session via `sessionGames` and `padelRowsFromGames`, reads raw state through `api.get`, computes standings, renders the round UI, validates scores with `sportScoreError` and `boardPoints`, submits via `logSportsGame`, and calls `refresh`. Business logic (round pairing and points tallying) is inseparable from the DOM code.
violations.fixPrompt: Extract the Americano session domain logic from `openSessionRunner` into pure functions — `buildRounds(session)`, `tallySessionPoints(games)` (reusing `padelRowsFromGames`), and `nextUnplayedRound(session, games)` — that take data and return values with no DOM access. Keep `openSessionRunner` for sheet wiring, and move score submission into a `submitRoundScore` function that validates and calls `logSportsGame` then `refresh`.

violations.title: `sportScoreError` is both the score validator and the application bootstrap
violations.content: The `sportScoreError` function mixes two abstraction levels in 22 statements: it performs low-level score comparison/validation (its name and its use from `sync`, `openGames`, and `openSessionRunner`), while also driving top-level application flow — `switchBoard`, `api.isUnlocked`, `api.lock`, `render`, `openPasscode`, and `refresh`. A validator that returns an error string should not be starting the app, toggling the lock, or opening modals.
violations.fixPrompt: Separate the two concerns: keep `sportScoreError(sport, a, b, target)` as a pure function returning an error string or `null`, and move the bootstrap/wiring code (`switchBoard`, `isUnlocked`/`lock`, `render`, `openPasscode`, `refresh`) into an explicit `init()` entry point invoked once at module load.

violations.title: UI module reaches into raw `api` state via `get()` instead of typed accessors
violations.content: `api` exposes a generic `get()` state accessor that `sportScoreError` calls from `padelRowsFromGames`, `combinedAllTime`, and the session-runner `draw` — and `api.loadBoard` itself calls `get()` eight times. The UI therefore navigates the raw board payload shape (games, sessions, players, nested rows) directly rather than going through an intentional interface, so any change to the response shape from the `admin` backend breaks scattered call sites in the UI with no compile-time or runtime signal.
violations.fixPrompt: Replace the generic `get()` accessor with named, intention-revealing selectors on `api` — e.g. `getGames()`, `getSportsGames()`, `getPlayers()`, `getSessions()`, `getBoard()` — that normalize the backend payload once. Update `padelRowsFromGames`, `combinedAllTime`, and the session-runner `draw` in the UI module to use those selectors and stop indexing into the raw response object.

violations.title: `padelRowsFromGames` computes standings from data it does not own
violations.content: `padelRowsFromGames` takes game data, pulls additional state out of the `api` module via `get()`, and resolves display names through `nameOf`, using no state of its own — 13 lines at nesting depth 3 of pure aggregation over another module's data structures. The points/standings computation belongs next to the padel session data, not in the UI module.
violations.fixPrompt: Move the standings aggregation in `padelRowsFromGames` into a `padel` domain module that receives games and players as explicit parameters and returns plain standings rows, with no calls back into `api.get`. Have the UI (`openSessionRunner`, `padelTableHTML`, `padelSpotlightHTML`) call that function with data it already holds and apply `nameOf` only at the presentation boundary.

violations.title: `ensureAudio` must be primed before `playLoserSound`, with no enforcement
violations.content: `ensureAudio` is invoked defensively at the top of `openLog`, `openLogSport`, and `openStartAmericano` purely so that a later `playLoserSound` works — the browser audio context can only be created during a user gesture. `playLoserSound` also calls `ensureAudio`, but by then the gesture may have passed, so the failure is silent: no sound plays and no error is reported. A new sheet that forgets the priming call will silently lose the loser sound.
violations.fixPrompt: Make the audio priming implicit rather than a call each sheet must remember: register a one-time `pointerdown`/`click` listener at startup that calls `ensureAudio` and unlocks the audio context, then remove the manual `ensureAudio` calls from `openLog`, `openLogSport`, and `openStartAmericano`. Have `playLoserSound` log or surface a warning when the context is still suspended instead of failing silently.

violations.title: `refresh` hides a required load-then-render ordering that callers can bypass
violations.content: `refresh` is the only place that sequences `loadBoards` → `loadBoard` → `render`, but `render` is also called directly by `switchBoard`, `attempt`, `openPasscode`, and the bootstrap in `sportScoreError`. Nothing prevents `render` from running against stale or never-loaded board state; the result is a page rendered from partial data with no error, and correctness depends on every caller remembering the right order.
violations.fixPrompt: Make the load/render ordering explicit in the UI module: keep a single state object with a `loaded` flag set only by `loadBoard`, and have `render` return early (or throw in development) when state has not been loaded. Route all display updates through `refresh`, or give `switchBoard`, `attempt`, and `openPasscode` an awaited `reload()` before they call `render` so ordering cannot be skipped.

violations.title: Domain identifiers, dates, sports, and scores are passed as bare primitives
violations.content: Board ids, player ids, and game ids are all plain `number` guarded by a single shared `isId`, dates are plain `string` re-validated by `isIsoDate` at six call sites, scores are plain `number` checked by `isScore` at four, and sport names are bare strings compared against literals in `cleanGameTypes` and `scoreError`. Signatures like `scoreError(sport: string, a: number, b: number, padelTarget)` make it easy to transpose arguments — `a` and `b` are interchangeable at the type level, as are board and player ids — and the same format checks are repeated inline throughout the handler.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce branded/nominal types in the `admin` module for the domain primitives — `BoardId`, `PlayerId`, `GameId`, `IsoDate`, `Score`, `SportName` — with a single parse function each (`parseBoardId`, `parseIsoDate`, `parseScore`, `parseSport`) that validates once at the request boundary and returns the branded value. Change `scoreError`, `cleanPoints`, and the action handlers to accept those types so ids and scores cannot be swapped, and delete the repeated inline `isId`/`isIsoDate`/`isScore` checks from the handler body.

violations.title: Client config mixes a copied config file, hostname sniffing, and a URL query param
violations.content:
`js/config.js` derives runtime settings from at least three different mechanisms in one small module: a checked-out copy of `js/config.example.js` (the file itself, holding literal values such as the Supabase URL/key), a hardcoded hostname allowlist (`['localhost', '127.0.0.1'].includes(...)`) used to infer the environment, and a URL query parameter (`new URLSearchParams(globalThis.location?.search ?? '').has(...)`) used to toggle mock mode.

Meanwhile the server side (`supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`) reads every setting from the environment via `Deno.env.get` (`ALLOWED_ORIGIN`, service keys, passcode). So the same application has two unrelated configuration systems, and within the browser half there is no single source of truth: whether the app talks to a real backend depends on which host it happens to be served from and on an ad-hoc query string, not on one declared setting.

This matters because environment inference by hostname silently breaks on any host not in the literal list (preview deploys, LAN IPs, custom dev domains), and because `config.js` is a manual copy of `config.example.js` — the two drift with no mechanism to detect a missing or stale key.
violations.fixPrompt: Unify client configuration in `js/config.js` into a single explicit config object with one declared source of truth per setting. Replace the hostname allowlist check (`['localhost', '127.0.0.1'].includes(...)`) and the query-param toggle (`new URLSearchParams(...).has(...)`) with an explicit exported flag (e.g. `USE_MOCK`) whose value is set in the config file itself, or injected at build time, rather than inferred from `location.hostname`. Keep the query param only as a documented developer override that reads the same named key. Add a startup validation step that asserts every key present in `js/config.example.js` also exists in `js/config.js`, and throws a clear error naming the missing key, so the example file and the real file cannot drift silently.

violations.title: Game types and default points target hardcoded inline in `js/api.js` instead of read from `./config.js`
violations.content:
`js/api.js` imports `./config.js` (for the mock toggle) but then defines domain configuration inline rather than sourcing it from that module: `ALL_TYPES = ['cards', 'tt_singles', 'tt_doubles', 'padel']` and the default `points_target: 21`, with the same `21` repeated later as an inline fallback in `logSportsGame` (`board(leaderboard_id)?.points_target ?? 21`).

The same list of game types is independently validated server-side in `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts` via `GAME_TYPES.includes(...)`, so the allowed-values list exists as a separate literal in two modules with two different mechanisms (inline array in the browser, module constant in the edge function). Adding or renaming a game type requires editing unrelated literals in both places, and a mismatch surfaces only as a rejected request at runtime.
violations.fixPrompt: Move the game-type list and the default padel points target out of `js/api.js` and into `js/config.js` as exported constants (e.g. `GAME_TYPES` and `DEFAULT_POINTS_TARGET`), then import them in `js/api.js` and use them in place of the inline `ALL_TYPES` array, the seeded `points_target: 21`, and the `?? 21` fallback in `logSportsGame`. Ensure `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts` validates against the same canonical list — either by sharing a small module both sides import, or by keeping one definition and documenting it as the source of truth — so the allowed game types are declared exactly once.
violations.snippet:
// No dependency: plain fetch is enough for a handful of tables.
import { SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, ADMIN_FN, USE_MOCK } from './config.js';

violations.title: `renameLeaderboard` also rewrites game types and points target
violations.content: `renameLeaderboard` is named as if it only changes a board's name, but it forwards `game_types` and `points_target` to the `rename_leaderboard` admin action as well — it is a full board-settings update. The caller in `app.js` (`openRenameBoard`, titled "Board settings") relies on exactly that wider behaviour, so the name understates the scope. The mock implementation at `js/api.js:115` has the same problem and additionally treats the extra fields as optional patches (`if (game_types?.length)`, `if (points_target)`), which diverges from what the real endpoint does with a `null`. A reader calling `renameLeaderboard(id, newName)` from a new call site would silently blank out or fail to preserve the board's game types.
violations.fixPrompt: Rename the exported `renameLeaderboard` in `js/api.js` (and its `mock.renameLeaderboard` counterpart) to something that reflects its real scope, e.g. `updateLeaderboard` or `saveBoardSettings`, and update the call site in `js/app.js` (`openRenameBoard`). Keep the wire-level `action` string `rename_leaderboard` unchanged so the Edge Function contract is untouched, or rename it on both sides consistently.
violations.snippet:
export const renameLeaderboard = (leaderboard_id, name, game_types, points_target) =>
  USE_MOCK ? mock.renameLeaderboard(leaderboard_id, name, game_types, points_target) : call('rename_leaderboard', { leaderboard_id, name, game_types, points_target });

violations.title: `SPORTS.padel.total` is never read
violations.content: The `total` field on the `SPORTS` metadata map is dead. Its only read site is `totalFor` at `js/app.js:422`: `const totalFor = (s) => (s === 'padel' ? padelTotal : SPORTS[s].total);`. For `padel` the expression short-circuits to `padelTotal` (the board's configured points-per-round), so `total: 21` here is unreachable; for every other sport the field is hardcoded `null`, so `SPORTS[s].total` always evaluates to `null`. The whole property therefore contributes nothing, and the stale `21` is actively misleading because it looks like the padel default while the real default lives in `boardPoints()` at `js/app.js:72`.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, remove the `total` property from every entry of the `SPORTS` map (lines 12-16) and simplify `totalFor` at line 422 to `const totalFor = (s) => (s === 'padel' ? padelTotal : null);`. Verify the only consumers are the `total != null` check in `sync()` at line 495 and the hint text at line 497.
violations.snippet: padel:      { label: 'Padel · Americano',      icon: '🎾', perSide: 2, total: 21 },

violations.title: `LUCK_BASELINE_SPORT` is imported but never used
violations.content: `LUCK_BASELINE_SPORT` is imported from `./ranking.mjs` but is never referenced anywhere in `js/app.js`. Only `LUCK_BASELINE` is used, in the card-table legend at line 1126. The racquet baseline is applied internally by `computeSportStandings` in `ranking.mjs`, so `app.js` has no need for the constant. The unused import suggests the per-sport legend was meant to state its own baseline and never got written — `sportTablesHTML` renders no baseline legend at all, unlike `tableHTML` and `padelTableHTML`.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, remove `LUCK_BASELINE_SPORT` from the import list on line 6. If the omission of a baseline legend in `sportTablesHTML` was unintentional, instead add a legend line to that table using `LUCK_BASELINE_SPORT` mirroring the one in `tableHTML` at line 1126.
violations.snippet: MODES, LUCK_BASELINE, LUCK_BASELINE_SPORT, MIN_GAMES_FOR_RATE,

violations.title: `!types.length` guard is always false
violations.content: `readGameTypes(box)` can never return an empty array: every entry in `GT_GROUPS` has a non-empty `types` list, and the lookup ends in `?? ['cards']` (`js/app.js:93`). The guard `if (!types.length) return;` is therefore always false and unreachable as a return path. The identical dead guard appears again in `openRenameBoard` at `js/app.js:224`. These are leftovers from when the picker was multi-select checkboxes (where an empty selection was possible) and were not removed when it became a single-choice radio — the comment at line 111 confirms the switch.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, delete the dead `if (!types.length) return;` guards on line 199 (`openNewBoard`) and line 224 (`openRenameBoard`), since `readGameTypes` always returns at least one type.
violations.snippet: if (!types.length) return;

violations.title: `need` is always the empty string
violations.content: `const need = '';` is a constant empty string that is interpolated into the row template at `js/app.js:1099` (`${need}`), where it can never render anything. The preceding comment explains the per-row "N more to rank" hint was deliberately dropped in favour of the divider row, but the now-inert variable and its interpolation were left behind. It is pure noise in a template that is otherwise dense.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, remove the `const need = '';` declaration on line 1089 and the `${need}` interpolation in the `who` cell on line 1099. Keep the explanatory comment on lines 1087-1088 if it is still useful, reworded to not reference a variable that no longer exists.
violations.snippet: const need = '';

violations.title: `goBtn.disabled = false` in `wireGamePicker` is a no-op
violations.content: `wireGamePicker`'s `sync()` unconditionally sets `goBtn.disabled = false`. Both call sites pass a button that is rendered without a `disabled` attribute (`js/app.js:192` "Create", `js/app.js:217` "Save") and nothing else ever disables them, so the assignment never changes state. The comment on lines 109-110 acknowledges this ("A radio always has exactly one selected, so Create stays enabled") — it is a leftover from the multi-select version of the picker where an empty selection had to disable the button. The `goBtn` parameter exists only to serve this dead assignment.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, remove `goBtn.disabled = false;` from `sync()` in `wireGamePicker` (line 116) and drop the now-unused `goBtn` parameter from the signature on line 111, updating the two call sites at lines 195 and 220 to `wireGamePicker(box)`.
violations.snippet: goBtn.disabled = false;

violations.title: Points-per-round bounds and default repeated as bare literals
violations.content: `readPoints` validates with bare literals `v >= 6 && v <= 99` and falls back to `21`. The same three numbers are hardcoded again in the input markup one function above (`min="6" max="99" value="${points ?? 21}"` at `js/app.js:100`), and the `21` default is repeated in at least three more places: `sportScoreError`'s `padelTarget = 21` parameter (`js/app.js:22`), `boardPoints()`'s `?? 21` (`js/app.js:72`), and the mock backend's `?? 21` (`js/api.js:143`). Nothing names what 6 and 99 are or why 21 is the default, and the duplication means a change to the allowed range must be made in two places that can silently drift apart — the HTML would accept a value the validator rejects, or vice versa.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, introduce named constants near the other module constants, e.g. `const PADEL_POINTS_MIN = 6, PADEL_POINTS_MAX = 99, PADEL_POINTS_DEFAULT = 21;`, and use them in both `pointsFieldHTML` (the `min`/`max`/`value` attributes on line 100) and `readPoints` (lines 105-107), plus `sportScoreError`'s default parameter on line 22 and `boardPoints()` on line 72. Export the default from a shared module if you also want `js/api.js:143` to reuse it rather than repeat the literal.

violations.title: Backend selected by sniffing the hostname at runtime
violations.content: Which Supabase project the app talks to is decided by an inline hostname check: `const isLocal = ['localhost', '127.0.0.1'].includes(globalThis.location?.hostname); const active = isLocal ? LOCAL : PROD;`. The environment is inferred from where the page happens to be served rather than from an explicit configuration value, and the branch fails open to production. Any host that is not literally `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` silently gets the live project — a LAN IP such as `192.168.1.x` when testing from a phone, `[::1]`, a `*.local` mDNS name, or a staging deployment. There is also no way to point a locally served page at production (or the reverse) for a deliberate smoke test without editing the file. `js/config.example.js:21-22` carries the identical pattern, so the template propagates it to every copy.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/config.js`, replace the hostname sniff with an explicit target selection: define a named map of environments (e.g. `const ENVS = { local: LOCAL, prod: PROD }`) and pick from it using an explicit override first — for example a `?env=local` URL parameter or a `globalThis.LOTD_ENV` value set by the page — falling back to the hostname heuristic only as a default. Keep the failure mode conservative and make the chosen environment visible (e.g. export it as `ACTIVE_ENV`) so it can be asserted in tests. Apply the same change to `js/config.example.js` so new copies inherit it.
violations.snippet:
const isLocal = ['localhost', '127.0.0.1'].includes(globalThis.location?.hostname);
const active = isLocal ? LOCAL : PROD;

violations.title: Unreachable 404 branch after `.single()` in `rename_leaderboard`
violations.content: The Supabase `.single()` modifier makes PostgREST return an error (code `PGRST116`, "JSON object requested, multiple (or no) rows returned") when the `update ... where id = leaderboard_id` matches zero rows — it does not return `data: null` with a null `error`. That means line 161 (`if (error) return bad(error.message)`) always fires first, and the `if (!data) return bad('leaderboard not found', 404)` on line 162 is unreachable. The practical consequence is that renaming a non-existent leaderboard returns HTTP 400 with a raw PostgREST message instead of the intended HTTP 404 with a friendly one.
violations.fixPrompt: In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, the `rename_leaderboard` case uses `.select().single()`, which returns a PostgREST error (`PGRST116`) rather than `data: null` when no row matches. Make the 404 path reachable: either switch the query to `.maybeSingle()` and keep the `if (!data) return bad('leaderboard not found', 404)` check, or keep `.single()` and detect the not-found case in the error branch (e.g. `if (error) return error.code === 'PGRST116' ? bad('leaderboard not found', 404) : bad(error.message)`), removing the now-dead `if (!data)` line.

violations.title: Unreachable 404 branch after `.single()` in `restore_player`
violations.content: Same pattern as `rename_leaderboard`: `.select().single()` on line 214 causes PostgREST to return an error (code `PGRST116`) when the `update ... where id = player_id` matches no rows, so line 215's `if (error) return bad(error.message)` always returns first. The `if (!data) return bad('player not found', 404)` on line 216 is dead code, and restoring a non-existent player yields a 400 with a raw PostgREST message rather than the intended 404.
violations.fixPrompt: In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, the `restore_player` case uses `.select().single()`, so a zero-row update surfaces as a PostgREST error (`PGRST116`), never as `data: null`. Make the 404 reachable: switch to `.maybeSingle()` and keep the `if (!data) return bad('player not found', 404)` check, or keep `.single()` and map `error.code === 'PGRST116'` to `bad('player not found', 404)` while deleting the dead `if (!data)` line.

violations.title: Padel default round target `21` hardcoded in multiple places
violations.content: The default padel round total is written as the bare literal `21` in four separate spots: the `padelTarget = 21` default parameter of `scoreError` (line 81), `board?.points_target ?? 21` (line 310), `scoreError(sport, score_a, score_b, padelTarget ?? 21)` (line 312), and `g.points_target ?? 21` in `edit_sports_score` (line 366). Unlike the badminton/table-tennis literals, which are explained by adjacent rules comments, this value is a product default that must stay in sync across all four sites and with the DB column default — changing the default in one place while missing another would silently validate rounds against two different targets. A named constant (e.g. `DEFAULT_PADEL_TARGET`) would make the intent explicit and keep the sites consistent.
violations.fixPrompt: In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, introduce a module-level `const DEFAULT_PADEL_TARGET = 21;` near the other constants (alongside `SPORTS` / `GAME_TYPES`), with a short comment noting it must match the `leaderboards.points_target` DB default. Replace the four bare `21` literals that represent the padel default: the `padelTarget = 21` default parameter in `scoreError` (line 81), `board?.points_target ?? 21` (line 310), `padelTarget ?? 21` (line 312), and `g.points_target ?? 21` (line 366). Leave the sport-rule literals for badminton (21/30/19/29) and table tennis (11/9) untouched — those are explained by their comments.

violations.title: Edge function `admin` has no error monitoring integration
violations.content:
The only import in this module is `https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2` — there is no Sentry, Bugsnag, Datadog, or OpenTelemetry SDK initialized. This is the sole server-side entry point of the application: it registers a handler via `Deno.serve` and fans out to database work (`Promise.all`), passcode verification (`crypto.subtle.digest`, `passcodeMatches`), and rate limiting (`fails.get`, `Date.now`). The visible error path consists only of the local `bad` and `json` helpers, which shape an HTTP response for the caller and report nothing outbound.

Because of that, a failure inside any handler branch — a Supabase query error, a malformed payload that slips past the `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/` and `Number.isInteger` guards, or an unhandled promise rejection inside `Promise.all` — surfaces to the user as a status code and then disappears. Deno Deploy captures stderr, but nothing aggregates, alerts on, or de-duplicates these, so a regression affecting every write request looks identical to normal operation from the outside.
violations.fixPrompt: In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, add error monitoring around the `Deno.serve` handler. Wrap the top-level handler body in a try/catch that reports the caught error to an external service before returning the existing `bad(...)` response, and register a global `unhandledrejection` listener that reports as well. Use a Deno-compatible SDK (for example `https://esm.sh/@sentry/deno`) initialized from a `SENTRY_DSN` read via `Deno.env.get`, and skip initialization when the variable is absent so local runs are unaffected. Include the request path and the resolved action name as context on each report, but do not attach the passcode or any hashed credential material.
violations.snippet: // LOTD admin Edge Function (v3) — the ONLY write path.

violations.title: Front end `app.js` has no client-side error reporting
violations.content:
`js/app.js` is the entire UI layer — it imports `./api.js`, `./export.mjs`, `./ranking.mjs`, and `./americano.mjs`, and drives the DOM directly (`document.createElement`, `box.querySelectorAll`, `r.addEventListener`). No error tracking SDK is imported here or in any sibling module, and there is no visible `globalThis.addEventListener('error', ...)` or `'unhandledrejection'` registration.

Every network call goes through `./api.js`, so a rejected fetch inside an event handler such as the `r.addEventListener` wiring becomes an unhandled rejection that the user sees only as a button that silently does nothing. Since this is a static client app with no server-rendered error page, there is no other channel through which such a failure could reach the maintainer.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/app.js`, register global handlers early in module initialization: `globalThis.addEventListener('error', ...)` and `globalThis.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ...)`, forwarding the error to an error tracking service. Gate initialization on a DSN value exported from `js/config.js` (and add the matching placeholder key to `js/config.example.js`) so that the mock/local mode driven by `USE_MOCK` does not report. As a minimum fallback if no external service is desired, surface these failures in the UI instead of letting them vanish.
violations.snippet: import * as api from './api.js';

violations.title: HTTP handler `Deno.serve` has no response time or query duration instrumentation
violations.content:
The `Deno.serve` handler in this module is the application's only HTTP server, and no metrics library (`prom-client`, StatsD, OpenTelemetry) appears among its imports — the sole import is `https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2`. The visible call list shows `Date.now` used only for rate-limit bookkeeping alongside `fails.get`, not for timing.

As a result, request latency is unmeasured, and the Supabase queries this function issues — including the fan-out under `Promise.all` and the aggregate reads backing the standings views — have no recorded duration. A query that degrades as the games and sports games tables grow, or a slow `crypto.subtle.digest` path under load, will not be visible until requests start timing out.
violations.fixPrompt: Instrument the `Deno.serve` handler in `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts` with timing: capture a start timestamp at the top of the handler, and on every exit path (including the `bad` error responses) record the elapsed duration together with the action name and response status. Also time the Supabase calls, especially the ones batched under `Promise.all`. Emit these either through an OpenTelemetry exporter or, if a full metrics backend is out of scope, as structured single-line records that Deno Deploy log ingestion can aggregate. Keep the instrumentation off the hot path when a metrics endpoint is not configured.
violations.snippet: // LOTD admin Edge Function (v3) — the ONLY write path.

violations.title: `get` performs Supabase REST reads with no retry on transient failures
violations.content: `get` is the shared read primitive for every Supabase REST call in the app, but the single `fetch` has no retry wrapper. Any transient condition — a dropped connection, DNS blip, mobile network handoff, or a `502`/`503`/`429` from the Supabase edge — throws immediately and surfaces to the user as "Couldn't reach the server". Because this is a `GET` with no side effects, retrying is fully safe and idempotent, so this is the highest-value place to add backoff: a couple of retries would absorb the majority of these failures invisibly. The current code also collapses the distinction between retryable (`5xx`, `429`, network error) and non-retryable (`4xx`) responses.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/api.js`, add retry-with-exponential-backoff to `get`. Wrap the `fetch` call in a loop of ~3 attempts. Retry when `fetch` itself rejects (network error) or when `res.status` is `429` or >= `500`; do not retry other `4xx` statuses — throw those immediately. Back off between attempts (e.g. 300ms, 600ms, 1200ms) with a small random jitter, and honour the `Retry-After` header if present on a `429`. After the final attempt, throw the existing `Couldn't reach the server (${res.status})` error so callers are unaffected. Consider extracting the retry loop into a small `fetchWithRetry` helper so it can be reused.
violations.snippet:
const res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${path}`, { headers: H });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Couldn't reach the server (${res.status})`);

violations.title: `call` invokes the admin edge function with no retry on transient failures
violations.content:
`call` is the single entry point for every admin action against the `ADMIN_FN` edge function, and it issues one `fetch` with no retry. Edge functions are especially prone to transient failures — cold starts, worker recycling, and boot timeouts routinely produce `503`/`504` responses that succeed on an immediate retry. Today any such blip fails the user's admin action outright.

Unlike `get`, this is a `POST` that mutates state, so a blanket retry is not safe: an action that actually applied server-side but whose response was lost would be applied twice. Retries here should be limited to cases where the request provably did not reach the handler — a `fetch` rejection or a `503`/`504` — or the actions should be made idempotent (e.g. a client-generated request id the handler de-duplicates on) before retrying more broadly.
violations.fixPrompt: In `js/api.js`, add narrow retry logic to `call`. Retry only on conditions where the request almost certainly did not apply server-side: a `fetch` rejection before any response, or `res.status` of `503`/`504`. Do not retry on other `5xx`, on `4xx`, or on a well-formed response where `out.ok` is false, since the mutation may have partially applied. Use ~2 retries with exponential backoff (e.g. 300ms then 900ms) plus jitter. For stronger safety, generate a unique request id per `call` invocation, include it in the JSON body, and de-duplicate on it in the admin edge function handler so retries become fully idempotent; only widen the retry conditions once that de-duplication is in place. Preserve the existing error messages and return value.

violations.title: `loadBoard` aborts the whole board load if any one of eight independent queries fails
violations.content:
`loadBoard` fetches eight independent datasets (`v_standings`, `v_sport_standings`, `v_padel_standings`, `games`, `sports_games`, `players`, `v_daily_losses`, `padel_sessions`) with `Promise.all`. A single rejection — a transient network error, a permissions issue on one view, or a missing/renamed table such as `padel_sessions` on a board that never plays padel — rejects the whole call, so the caller sees a total load failure and the UI renders nothing.

These sections are independent: card standings do not depend on padel sessions, and the daily-loss panel does not depend on the sports game log. The batch should report partial success so the sections that did load still render, with only the failed section showing an error or empty state.
violations.fixPrompt: In `loadBoard` in `js/api.js`, replace `Promise.all` with `Promise.allSettled` over the eight `get(...)` calls. Map each settled result to its `value` on fulfilment and to a safe empty default (`[]`) on rejection, and collect the rejection reasons into an `errors` field on the returned object (e.g. `{ standings, sportStandings, ..., errors }`) so callers can surface a per-section warning instead of failing the entire board render. Keep the existing `USE_MOCK` short-circuit and the returned property names unchanged so existing consumers keep working.
violations.snippet:
const [standings, sportStandings, padelStandings, games, sportsGames, players, dailyLosses, padelSessions] = await Promise.all([
    get(`v_standings?select=player_id,name,gp,losses,archived&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=name`),
    get(`v_sport_standings?select=sport,player_id,name,games,losses,archived&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&sport=neq.cards&order=name`),
    get(`v_padel_standings?select=player_id,name,archived,rounds,points_for,points_against&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=name`),
    get(`games?select=id,game_date,p1,p2,p3,p4,loser,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc`),
    get(`sports_games?select=id,game_date,sport,a1,a2,b1,b2,score_a,score_b,points_target,session_id,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc`),
    get(`players?select=id,name,archived&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=name`),
    get(`v_daily_losses?select=player_id,name,losses&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&game_date=eq.${today}`),
    get(`padel_sessions?select=id,game_date,roster,courts,rounds,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=created_at.desc`),
  ]);
  return { standings, sportStandings, padelStandings, games, sportsGames, players, dailyLosses, padelSessions };

violations.title: `loadBoard` fetches unbounded `games` and `sports_games` history with no `limit`
violations.content:
The `games` and `sports_games` queries inside `loadBoard` specify `order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc` but no `limit` or range header, so every call materializes the board's **entire** game history into an in-memory array. This collection has no size cap and grows monotonically for the life of the leaderboard.

The growth is amplified by how often it runs: `refresh()` calls `loadBoard()` and is invoked after every single write — every logged card game, every racquet game, and notably after *each individual match* in the Americano round-runner (`openSessionRunner` calls `await refresh(); draw();` on each `Log` tap). So a single padel night re-downloads and re-parses the full history dozens of times, each time larger than the last.

Downstream consumers hold the whole array too: `openGames()` builds `merged()` from all of `data.games` plus all of `data.sportsGames` and writes every row into `rows.innerHTML` in one shot, and `rowsHTML` calls `losingStreak(data?.games ?? [], p.player_id)` once per player over the full array. On a long-lived board viewed from a phone, the unbounded payload plus the unbounded DOM render is the realistic memory/latency failure point.

Add server-side pagination (a `limit` on the initial load, with an explicit "load more" for the history sheet) so the in-memory collection has a bounded size independent of how long the board has existed.
violations.fixPrompt:
In `loadBoard` in `js/api.js`, bound the two history queries so the in-memory arrays cannot grow without limit. Add an explicit `limit` to the `games` and `sports_games` PostgREST queries (e.g. `&limit=200`), since both already sort newest-first via `order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc`. Introduce a named constant such as `HISTORY_LIMIT` at module scope rather than inlining the number.

Then make the truncation visible instead of silent: have `openGames()` in `js/app.js` render a "Load older games" affordance when the returned page is full (length === HISTORY_LIMIT), fetching the next page via a new paginated read helper that accepts an offset. Ensure the mock backend in `api.js` honours the same limit so demo mode matches production behaviour.

Also confirm that the aggregate views (`v_standings`, `v_sport_standings`, `v_padel_standings`, `v_daily_losses`) are still the source of truth for all standings numbers, so limiting the raw game arrays cannot change any displayed ranking. The one place that consumes raw `data.games` for a computed value is `losingStreak` in `rowsHTML` — verify a truncated array still yields a correct streak, or cap the streak computation explicitly.
violations.snippet:
get(`games?select=id,game_date,p1,p2,p3,p4,loser,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc`),
    get(`sports_games?select=id,game_date,sport,a1,a2,b1,b2,score_a,score_b,points_target,session_id,created_at&leaderboard_id=eq.${id}&order=game_date.desc,created_at.desc`),

violations.title: `rosterMem` is a module-level cache with no size limit or eviction policy
violations.content:
`rosterMem` is a module-scoped object used as a cache of the last-used A/B roster split, keyed by `${boardId}:${sport}` and written on every successful racquet save (`rosterMem[memKey()] = { a: [...a], b: [...b] }` in the `save` handler of `openLogSport`). Entries are only ever added — nothing removes them, and there is no maximum entry count.

In practice the key space is bounded by (number of boards) × (5 sports), and each value holds at most four integer ids, so this will not realistically exhaust memory in a browser tab. It is flagged as a hygiene issue rather than a crash risk: the cache also never invalidates when a board is deleted via `openDeleteBoard`, so stale roster entries for deleted boards persist for the lifetime of the page.

A bounded structure with explicit eviction would make the growth characteristics obvious and drop entries for boards that no longer exist.
violations.fixPrompt:
In `js/app.js`, convert `rosterMem` from a bare object into a bounded LRU-style cache. Replace it with a `Map` (which preserves insertion order) and add a small helper that, on write, deletes the existing key before re-inserting it and then evicts the oldest entry while `size` exceeds a named constant such as `ROSTER_MEM_MAX` (a value like 20 is ample). Update the read in `restore()` and the write in the `save` handler of `openLogSport` to use `.get()`/`.set()` through that helper.

Additionally, clear entries for a deleted board: in `openDeleteBoard`, after the delete succeeds, remove every `rosterMem` key whose `boardId` prefix matches the deleted board so stale rosters do not survive the board itself.
violations.snippet:
let lastSport = 'tt_singles';
const rosterMem = {};   // `${boardId}:${sport}` -> { a:[ids], b:[ids] }

violations.title: Rate-limit map `fails` grows without bound and has no eviction
violations.content:
`fails` is a module-level `Map` keyed by client IP that acts as an in-memory cache for the brute-force lockout, but it has no size cap, no TTL sweep, and no eviction policy. An entry is added on every failed passcode attempt (`fails.set(ip, ...)`, line 124) and is only ever removed on a *successful* passcode (`fails.delete(ip)`, line 128). Entries whose `until` timestamp has already expired are never reclaimed — the lockout check at line 116 reads `rec.until > now` but leaves the stale record in place, so the map only grows for the lifetime of the Edge Function instance.

The key is derived from the `x-forwarded-for` header (line 113), which is request-controlled. Anyone who can reach the function can send POSTs with a wrong passcode and a fresh spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` value each time, inserting an unbounded number of distinct keys — and the per-IP lockout never engages, because every request lands on a brand-new key. Each entry is small, but with no upper bound the map grows linearly with request volume until the isolate hits its memory limit and the function crashes, taking down the only write path for the app.

Even without a malicious actor, ordinary traffic from many distinct client IPs (mobile networks rotate addresses) accumulates entries indefinitely, since only successfully-authenticated IPs are ever deleted.
violations.fixPrompt:
In `supabase/functions/admin/index.ts`, bound the in-memory `fails` map so it cannot grow without limit.

1. Add a `MAX_TRACKED = 10_000` (or similar) constant alongside `MAX_FAILS` and `LOCK_MS`.
2. Store a `seen: number` timestamp on each record so counters that never reached `MAX_FAILS` can be aged out.
3. Before inserting a new entry in the failure path (`fails.set(ip, ...)` near line 124), sweep expired records: iterate `fails` and `delete` any entry whose `until` is `0` or `<= now` and whose `seen` is older than `LOCK_MS`.
4. After the sweep, if `fails.size >= MAX_TRACKED`, evict the oldest entries (or clear the map) before adding the new one, so the map has a hard ceiling regardless of traffic.
5. Also `fails.delete(ip)` in the lockout check around line 116 when `rec.until <= now`, so expired lockouts are reclaimed on read as well.

Keep the existing behaviour otherwise: 5 wrong passcodes still triggers a 60s cooldown, and a correct passcode still clears the counter.
violations.snippet: const fails = new Map<string, { n: number; until: number }>();

violations.title: Module-level `data` cache is only refreshed on local writes, so remote changes and the date rollover never invalidate it
violations.content:
`data` (declared at line 49) holds the entire board payload — `standings`, `games`, `sportsGames`, `players`, `dailyLosses`, `padelSessions` — and is only repopulated by `loadBoard()` when `refresh()` or `switchBoard()` is called. Both are triggered exclusively by local user actions (initial `refresh()` at line 1221, a board switch, or a successful write from this tab).
